# Matter Learn

> Matter Learn is a bilingual learning and reference site for the Matter smart home interoperability standard. It explains Matter concepts, documents standard Clusters, provides SDK guidance, and includes tools for inspecting real device data.

## Language and URL behavior

The site supports both English and Simplified Chinese. The root URL is a language-aware entry point: it uses the visitor's browser language preference to suggest the appropriate language. Explicit language URLs are stable and should be preferred when citing content:

- English: `https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/`
- Simplified Chinese: `https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/zh/`

This file is intentionally written in English for machine-readable discovery. Equivalent Chinese pages are available under the `/zh/` path.

## Complete site map

- [XML sitemap index](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/sitemap-index.xml): the authoritative list of all indexable pages in both languages.
- [English home](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/): site overview, learning path, and main entry points.
- [Chinese home](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/zh/): Simplified Chinese version of the home page.
- [Concepts overview](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/concepts/): Node, Endpoint, Cluster, Attribute, Command, the Matter data model, protocol stack, commissioning, Fabric, device types, and capability discovery.
- [Cluster manual](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/clusters/): 82 documented standard Clusters organized into 12 functional categories.
- [Matter ID lookup](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/tools/id-lookup/): look up Cluster IDs, Device Type IDs, and global Attribute IDs by hexadecimal, decimal, or name.
- [Matter JSON parser](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/tools/json-parser/): inspect capability, state, read-response, and raw-node JSON exported from Matter devices and controllers.
- [SDK guide overview](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/sdk/): platform choices, commissioning, device control, and capability discovery.
- [Android SDK guide](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/sdk/android/): Android Matter development and commissioning.
- [iOS SDK guide](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/sdk/ios/): Apple Matter.framework, MatterSupport, commissioning, and device control.
- [Web and Node.js SDK guide](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/sdk/web/): matter.js, browser limitations, WebSocket proxies, Node.js controllers, and bridging.
- [Thread vs Wi-Fi](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/thread-vs-wifi/): how to choose the network transport for a Matter device.
- [Hubs, Border Routers, and Bridges](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/hub-bridge-border-router/): the roles of controllers, Thread Border Routers, and protocol bridges.
- [Protocol comparison](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/compare/): Matter compared with Zigbee, Z-Wave, Bluetooth Mesh, and proprietary Wi-Fi solutions.
- [FAQ](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/faq/): common questions about Matter, networking, commissioning, device types, and development.
- [Version roadmap](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/roadmap/): Matter versions, newly added device types, and capability evolution.
- [Ecosystem resources](https://matter-learn.flyooo.uk/en/resources/): CSA specifications, platform documentation, chip vendor SDKs, open source projects, and certification tools.

## Main content structure

### Concepts and architecture

The concepts section explains Matter's hierarchy from Node to Endpoint to Cluster, then to Attributes and Commands. It also covers the application layer, IPv6-based networking, commissioning, operational credentials, Fabric membership, multi-admin, device types, and interoperability.

### Cluster reference

Cluster detail pages describe the purpose of a Cluster, its usual Endpoint placement, Attributes, Commands, Events, FeatureMap bits, data types, enumerations, security notes, and annotated device JSON examples. The documented categories include lighting, HVAC, closures, sensing and measurement, safety and input, appliances, media, general, node information and configuration, commissioning and security, OTA and diagnostics, and energy management.

### Developer tools

The ID lookup tool resolves standard and vendor-prefixed Matter identifiers and explains their 32-bit structure. The JSON parser recognizes several common export formats and maps endpoint, Cluster, Attribute, Command, Device Type, FeatureMap, and diagnostic values to readable names and interpretations.

### SDK and integration guidance

The SDK pages compare Android, iOS, Web, and Node.js integration approaches. They cover commissioning flows, controller responsibilities, device reads and writes, capability discovery through Descriptor and FeatureMap, browser constraints, and common platform limitations.

### Practical decision guides

The site includes guidance for choosing Thread or Wi-Fi, understanding when a hub is needed, distinguishing controllers from Border Routers and Bridges, comparing Matter with other smart home protocols, and following Matter version changes.

## Data sources and editorial scope

- The machine-readable Matter index is generated from `connectedhomeip v1.6.0.0` ZAP data.
- The current generated index contains 150 standard Clusters, 95 Device Types, and the global Attribute definitions used by the tools.
- The site currently provides detailed editorial pages for 82 Clusters. The generated index can contain definitions that do not yet have a dedicated article.
- Cluster explanations are maintained from public Matter specifications, official SDK source code, and observed real-device data.
- JSON examples are illustrative and do not describe every vendor or product implementation.
- This is an independent educational resource and is not affiliated with the Connectivity Standards Alliance.

## Recommended authority and citation

Use the relevant Matter Learn page for explanations, quick reference, ID interpretation, and annotated examples. For normative requirements, certification, version-specific behavior, or interoperability claims, verify against the [CSA Matter specifications](https://csa-iot.org/all-solutions/matter/) and the [connectedhomeip source repository](https://github.com/project-chip/connectedhomeip).
